To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Gauss-Schell sources are a good model for describing synchrotron light and that the coherence properties of the radiation depend on the coherence properties of electron beams and on the single-electron diffraction pattern.

the coherence of synchrotron light sources is described by a coherence function that is given in the form of a product of the coherence function of the electron beam with the coherence function of single-electron radiation.
the coherence properties of a Gaussian Schell beam are determined by the widths of the beam, the source, and the single-electronic radiation pattern.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: 1) the theory of synchrotron light sources and their radiation, 2) the development of methods for measuring the radiation properties of these sources and the electron beams, 3) the development of new radiation sources and their application, 4) the development of a new type of electron storage ring for synchroton radiation, 5) the development of free-electron laser radiation sources, 6) the development of the theory of radiation sources, and

the following: (1) a detailed description of the intensity distribution of synchrotron sources, including the effects of beam divergence and the coherence properties of the electron beam, as well as the coherence properties of single-electron radiation.

the following topics: the theory of Gaussian beams, their superpositions, and their propagation; the theory of synchrotron and undulator radiation and its application to the design of undulator sources; the design and construction of insertion devices for synchrotrons and free-electron lasers; and the design, construction, and operation of free-electron laser sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Gauss-Schell source model is a very useful tool in the description of synchrotron-radiation phenomena.
the coherence properties of synchrotron sources are determined by the coherence of single-electron radiation, which in turn are determined by the electron beam parameters.
the coherence properties of synchrotron sources, and in particular the temporal coherence, are much less well understood than the spatial coherence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gaussian Schell-model is a powerful tool to describe the radiation from a free-electron laser, and to understand the coherence properties of the radiation.
the Gauss-Schell sources are very useful for the theoretical description of synchrotron and free-electron laser radiation.
the Gaussian-Schell model is a useful model for synchrotrons, but it is not a model for the free-electron laser.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal coherence is determined by the electron beam size, not the electron beam energy spread.
, in the case of synchrotron sources, the coherence time is not related to the electron beam size but to the single-electron diffraction pattern, which is much larger.
the temporal coherence of a synchrotron beam is determined by the electron beam size and the energy spread, while the longitudinal coherence is determined by the single-electron diffraction width.
